You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The supplied input cell is a nonstandard 20-atom setting with lattice parameters a = 7.55239864 Å, b = 7.55239864 Å, c = 7.55239864 Å, α = 137.09853607°, β = 102.27344978°, and γ = 93.14694167°, containing Zn₄Si₄O₁₂. The structure is described in space group Ibam, number 72, with Hall symbol −I 2 2c. Fractional coordinates in the standard and input frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where P has rows (0.5, −0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5000000000000001, −0.5000000000000001), and (−0.5, 0.5000000000000001, 0.5000000000000001), and the origin shift s is (−8.326672684688674×10⁻¹⁷, 2.7755575615628914×10⁻¹⁷, 2.7755575615628914×10⁻¹⁷), effectively zero. The listed positions are rounded to six digits before applying the small corrections noted below.

In the standard Ibam description, zinc occupies the eightfold Wyckoff orbit 8g with coordinate relation (0, y, 1/4) and representative position (0, 0.290828, 0.25), so the only free zinc parameter is y = 0.290828. Silicon occupies the eightfold 8j orbit with relation (x, y, 0), represented by (0.2196134999999999, 0.08092949999999988, 0), giving independent parameters x = 0.2196134999999999 and y = 0.08092949999999988. Oxygen is distributed over three independent eightfold orbits. The first oxygen orbit is 8f, with relation (x, 0, 1/4), representative (0.18710099999999996, 0, 0.25), and free parameter x = 0.18710099999999996. The second oxygen orbit is 8j, with relation (x, y, 0), representative (0.11378599999999993, 0.2051560000000001, 0), and independent parameters x = 0.11378599999999993 and y = 0.2051560000000001. The third oxygen orbit is another distinct 8j set, also of the form (x, y, 0), represented by (0.11350900000000008, 0.621599, 0), with x = 0.11350900000000008 and y = 0.621599. Thus the conventional-cell content is generated from one Zn orbit, one Si orbit, and three crystallographically distinct O orbits, each of multiplicity eight.

The precision corrections apply to silicon positions expressed in the original input frame and preserve the real input geometry rather than forcing it onto an exactly idealized lattice. A silicon atom at input fractional position (0.300543, 0.080929, 0.219613) is displaced by (0, 0, +1.000000000001×10⁻⁶). A second silicon atom at (0.861316, 0.580929, 0.280387) is displaced by (0, 0, −9.999999999732445×10⁻⁷). A third silicon atom at (0.699457, 0.919071, 0.780387) is displaced by (0, 0, −1.0000000000287557×10⁻⁶). Together with the stated frame transformation, these values allow the original 20-atom input-cell geometry to be recovered while retaining the Ibam standard-setting description of the symmetry-generated structure.
